name: alchemical factor extraction method that takes a composite integer
notes:
Auto-designed from: Design an Ob3ect for:

alchemical factor extraction method that takes a composite integer and returns its prime factors

phase_0.boundary_condition: the sealed crucible containing the complete prime factorization
phase_0.domain_name: alchemical factor extraction method that takes a composite integer
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.justification: forward morphism: the divisor is confirmed as a factor and the quotient advances

AREV.justification: reverse morphism: the candidate is rejected and the search descends to the next divisor

CLINK.chosen_element: successive division steps chained by the current quotient
CLINK.justification: composition: each confirmed factor reduces the quotient for the next trial

ENGAGR.chosen_element: square of the candidate equals the current quotient
ENGAGR.justification: both arms hold: the candidate divides exactly once and the quotient becomes the same prime

EVALF.justification: negative arm: the candidate does not divide the current quotient

EVALT.justification: affirmative arm: the candidate divides the current quotient

FFUSE.chosen_element: verified factor or rejected candidate rejoining the search
FFUSE.justification: arms rejoin into the single state of the updated quotient and factor list

FSPLIT.justification: splits into the divides arm and the does-not-divide arm

IFIX.chosen_element: prime factor inscribed on the factor tablet
IFIX.justification: permanent, append-only record of a confirmed prime factor

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: a prime factor recognized as indivisible
IMSCRIB.justification: identity: the factor is itself and requires no further division

TANCH.chosen_element: sealed crucible holding the full factor list
TANCH.justification: the closed boundary that contains the finished factorization

VINIT.chosen_element: composite integer placed in the crucible
VINIT.justification: the unworked matter before any divisor is tested

phase_2.fuse_element: verified factor or rejected candidate rejoining the search
phase_2.fuse_result: updated quotient and factor list carried to the next candidate
phase_2.rejoin_note: on the divides arm the factor is fixated and the quotient reduces; on the does-not-divide arm the candidate increments; both arms rejoin into the single search state. the fork closes when the quotient reaches one.
phase_2.split_input: current quotient and the next candidate divisor
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — both held at once: candidate squared equals quotient, factor and quotient coincide
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10) — constructively refuted: a divisor that yields non-zero remainder
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01) — constructively proven: a divisor that yields zero remainder
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — neither: the composite integer before any divisor is tested
